thread.title: OhioHealth patients can access their medical records in latest version of Apple's Health app

author: Carrie Ghose
title: OhioHealth patients can access their medical records in latest version of Apple's Health app
text: – Staff reporter, Columbus Business First Feb 5, 2018, 12:30pm EST OhioHealth patients can access their medical records and test results on their iPhones with the latest release of Apple Inc .'s mobile operating system. The 10-hospital Columbus system was among a dozen nationwide that Apple chose for a beta test of the feature, along with Johns Hopkins Medicine in Baltimore, Cedars-Sinai in Los Angeles and Rush University Medical Center in Chicago. “This is one more layer in which people can engage with their information," said Salil Verma , OhioHealth's vice president of digital experience. “This is absolutely in line with well care." Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) h as increased its activity in health IT , including acquiring a company that aggregates health data, launching a heart study with Stanford University using Apple Watch and opening up ways to develop health-related iOS apps, according to our sister paper San Francisco Business Times . I've left messages with Apple seeking comment on how it selected health systems to pilot medical records access. Clues can be found in OhioHealth's increasing digital presence, such as creating Verma's position a year ago. He has worked for OhioHealth since 2010 and was promoted from senior IT manager. The IT department employs user experience designers and software developers. "We have invested in an engineering shop that brings these technologies to life," Verma said. "Very few (health systems) have this level of investment." OhioHealth has its own app that makes online scheduling and bill-payment easier. Late last year, it connected to Amazon.com Inc.'s Alexa, so users can ask questions such as how long the wait is at nearby urgent care centers. More than six years ago, the system hired Columbus-based Duet Health and provided content for a mobile app for patient education , such as weekly reminders during pregnancy. “That was the very start of leveraging digital technologies to engage with the customer," Verma said. Apple's Health app uses Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resource, a standard that web engineers follow to better enable exchanging health information from different records systems. Records access will appear when iPhone users update to iOS 11.3. They have to register with OhioHealth's online patient portal to establish login credentials. The system is open to partnerships with independent physicians for patients to access their records, Verma said. “We need to take seriously that they need to have a feeling that this experience was a pleasant one, and – this may be a bit ambitious – but we’re going for a delightful one," he said. – Staff reporter, Columbus Business First Feb 5, 2018, 12:30pm EST Related Content
